items.headline: Anthropic's Claude Autonomously Discovers CRISPR-Like Enzyme System (ART)
bullets: Claude autonomously identified array-associated reverse transcriptases (ART) in bacteriophage DNA after searching 1.9 billion protein clusters—a novel enzyme system structurally reminiscent of CRISPR arrays.
950 parallel AI agents spent 21.5 hours combing DNA sequences, consuming 215.6 million tokens, marking the first major output from Anthropic's spring-2026 life sciences lab in the Bay Area.

The system exhibits characteristics—DNA repeat arrays paired with a reverse transcriptase and accessory protein—found only in known programmable molecular machines, suggesting potential as a new gene-editing mechanism, though its actual function remains unknown.
MIT CRISPR pioneer Feng Zhang reviewed the preprint and called the discovery 'intriguing' and meriting further investigation, validating the autonomous discovery workflow.
Anthropic is inviting scientific proposals to determine ART's function and demonstrate AI-human collaboration in biological research at scale.
items.novelty: First public demonstration of Claude autonomously discovering a previously uncharacterized enzyme system in novel time: this represents a concrete proof-of-concept for AI agents systematizing biological discovery, moving beyond theoretical capability claims.

items.headline: F5 BIG-IP APM Zero-Day (CVE-2026-94127) Under Active Exploit as Critical RCE
bullets: Unauthenticated attackers exploit CVE-2026-94127, a 9.8 CVSS heap buffer overflow in F5 BIG-IP APM, to achieve remote code execution on systems configured as OAuth authorization servers.

The vulnerability affects only BIG-IP instances where APM serves as an OAuth server with an access policy and authorization server profile on the same virtual server—a specific but common enterprise setup.

F5 disclosed the flaw on September 22 with engineering hotfixes available; the attack vector bypasses management interface access controls because malicious traffic targets the virtual server directly.
Practical impact is high: no workaround available short of reconfiguring BIG-IP architecture or disabling OAuth on vulnerable instances.
items.novelty: New active exploitation of a recently disclosed critical RCE in widely deployed enterprise infrastructure—the specific OAuth configuration requirement makes this a targeted but high-impact threat for cloud/identity providers.

items.headline: Three Linux Kernel CVEs Actively Exploited; CISA Emergency Deadline Passed
bullets: CISA added CVE-2025-39682, CVE-2026-53266 (ebtables SNAT ARP out-of-bounds write, CVSS 8.8), and CVE-2025-39964 (AF_ALG race condition, CVSS 7.8) to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on September 18, triggering 3-day remediation windows now expired.

CVE-2026-53266 and CVE-2025-39964 allow local attackers to trigger DoS, privilege escalation, or cryptographic operation corruption via concurrent socket writes or network address translation rule manipulation.
Red Hat confirmed active exploitation as of September 19; no public disclosure yet of attack chains, but federal civilian agencies faced mandatory patching deadline that passed September 21.
Remediation required immediately on all systems; no practical workarounds available for network-exposed hosts beyond patching.
items.source: The Hacker News, Qualys, CISA KEV Catalog
items.novelty: Rare CISA emergency directive for Linux kernel flaws with immediate enforcement deadline now lapsed—indicates coordinated exploitation campaign or sophisticated tooling already in circulation.
